q: What are the terms of the hybrid fee option for Kaveri's PMS?
reference: 1.0% p.a. management fee plus 20% of returns above a 10% p.a. hurdle, with a high-water mark.

A.answer: The hybrid option (Option B) charges a 1.0% p.a. management fee plus a 20% performance fee on returns above a 10% p.a. hurdle, subject to a high-water mark [1][2][3]. Management fees are charged quarterly on daily average AUM, while the performance fee is charged annually on the account anniversary or on full withdrawal [4][3]. GST applies at the prevailing rate, operating expenses (custody, fund accounting, demat, audit) are capped at 0.25% p.a., brokerage is at actuals, and exit loads are 3% in year 1, 2% in year 2, and 1% in year 3 [1][4][3]. Clients may switch between Option A and Option B once a year, effective from the next anniversary date [1][3].

q: What counts as a SEV1 incident and how fast must on-call respond?
reference: A customer-wide outage or suspected data breach; response within 15 minutes, with the CISO and CTO paged.

A.answer: SEV1 covers a customer-wide outage, or a suspected data breach [1]; the Incident Reporting Procedure defines it as a customer-wide outage or a confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data [2]. On-call must acknowledge and start working within 15 minutes, 24x7 [1][2].

cited.title: SEV1 Incident Response Runbook
cited.text:
## 2. Severity levels

| Severity | Definition | Response time | Who is paged |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Customer-wide outage, or data breach suspected | 15 min | Primary + secondary on-call, Incident Commander rota, CISO and CTO |
| SEV2 | Service degraded for many customers (slow, partial features down) | 30 min | Primary on-call, Engineering Manager |
| SEV3 | Single customer impacted | 4 h | Primary on-call (business hours escalation) |
| SEV4 | Minor issue, no customer impact | Next business day | Ticket only |

When in doubt, declare the higher severity. Downgrading later is free; a late SEV1 is not.

cited.text:
## 5. Severity classification

The SOC or on-call incident commander assigns the severity. Severity can be raised or lowered as more is learnt.

| Severity   | Definition                                                                           | Response time     | Who is engaged                                                       |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SEV1       | Customer-wide outage, or confirmed breach of Confidential/Restricted data            | 15 minutes        | Incident commander; CISO and CTO paged; Head of Infrastructure & SRE |
| SEV2       | Significant degradation affecting many customers, or a contained security compromise | 30 minutes        | Incident commander, service owner, SOC lead                          |
| SEV3       | Issue affecting a single customer or user, or a policy violation without data loss   | 4 hours           | Service team or SOC analyst                                          |
| SEV4       | Minor issue, no customer impact                                                      | Next business day | Owning team via ticket                                               |

Response time means the time within which a responder acknowledges and starts working, 24x7 for SEV1 and SEV2, and during business hours for SEV3 and SEV4.

q: What did IC 48 decide about Vindhyagiri Cementworks and why?
reference: The Small Cap fund was to exit its entire Vindhyagiri Cementworks position due to governance concerns, in an orderly way by 15 May 2026, and the stock was put on the do-not-buy list for at least 24 months.

A.answer: IC 48 resolved to exit the Kaveri Small Cap Opportunities fund’s entire position in Vindhyagiri Cementworks Ltd by 15 May 2026 in an orderly manner (selling no more than 30 % of daily traded volume) and to place the stock on the “do not buy” list for all schemes for at least 24 months [1][2][3]. The decision was driven by governance concerns: the statutory auditor resigned in February 2026 citing inadequate information on related‑party transactions, ₹186 crore of advances to a promoter‑group entity lacked shareholder approval, and promoter pledges rose from 18 % to 46 % in nine months [4]. The committee concluded the investment thesis (regional cement consolidation) no longer outweighed these risks [1].
